# Changelog

What changed in each plugin release, newest first. In an agent, ask for `beau-help new`.

## bstack 0.20.0 (2026-11-19)

- `quality.py summary --json` now reports where CI time goes outside the test suite: a `lifecycle` object per repo (run and queue times, time outside the suite counted run by run, slowest and failing steps; a run counts in the week of its first job), from the job books. It appears only once the job books are adopted; without them the output is unchanged.

## bstack 0.19.0 (2026-11-19)

- `quality.py ingest` now books each run's `jobs.json` into `books/jobs.csv` and `books/steps.csv`, and `check` holds both files to rules, once the books have both files. `ingest --only jobs` books just the jobs and steps. Without the two files nothing changes: books written before them check, ingest, fetch and summarize exactly as before.

## bstack 0.18.0 (2026-11-19)

- `interrogate` gives every adversary the repo's `REVIEW.md`, read from the default branch, so a change can't rewrite the guide it is reviewed by. Claude Code Review reads the same file.
- A second `interrogate` round on the same scope starts from the first round's verified and dropped findings. Each finding now has a severity: Important, Nit or Pre-existing (it fails on the merge base too, and its fix gets its own PR).
- `scaffold-product` adds a starter `REVIEW.md`, and adopt mode drafts one from past review fixes.
- Try: `Interrogate this branch, then interrogate it again after I fix what you find.`

## bstack 0.17.0 (2026-11-19)

- `quality.py summary --json` now groups each repo's tests, their cost and their catches by test kind (`unit`, `e2e`, `property`, `differential`) under `by_kind`. Kinds come from an optional hand-edited `books/kinds.csv` (`repo,prefix,kind`, longest dotted prefix wins); books without it are valid and every test is `unit`. `check` validates the file's form only.

## bstack 0.16.0 (2026-11-18)

- `quality.py fetch` now stores what GitHub reports for each run's jobs and steps as `jobs.json`, once the books have a `books/jobs.csv`. Without that file nothing changes. A failed jobs call fails only that run's jobs and never stops its test artifacts.

## bstack 0.15.0 (2026-11-18)

- Every commit an agent writes now says how it was checked, in a `Verified:` git trailer: `receipt <run-id>`, `verify-work`, `tests` or `none <reason>`. The Opening a PR playbook defines the values, and beau-agent and verify-work carry the rule.
- `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Verified,valueonly)'` lists the stamp beside each commit, so unverified commits can be counted.
- Try: `Show me how each commit on this branch was verified.`

## bstack 0.14.0 (2026-11-18)

- `quality.py summary --json` now lists, per repo, `caught_on_pr`: the tests that failed in a pull request run that week, with the evidence link for each failure and a count of distinct tests, beside `failed_on_main`. The books and their checks are unchanged.

## bstack 0.13.1 (2026-11-16)

- `check-product.py --receipts` no longer accepts a receipt for a criterion whose text or probe was rewritten afterward, and `receipt.py` records INCONCLUSIVE when an untracked file was present before the probe.
- Ticking two boxes in turn, updating `ROADMAP.md` and the other record files, or renaming a spec no longer makes a receipt fail. A receipt whose commit is missing from the clone now says to run the probe again.

## bstack 0.13.0 (2026-11-16)

- A checked spec criterion now has a receipt: a ledger entry saying which probe ran, on which commit, and what came back. verify-work's `scripts/receipt.py` runs the probe and writes it, so the verdict comes from the exit code.
- A PR that moves criteria carries the `ledger receipts` table in its Verification section, and the Product phase playbook checks a box only on a VERIFIED receipt.
- `check-product.py --receipts <run-id>` fails when a box was checked without a VERIFIED receipt, or when the code changed after the probe ran. Needs agent-ledger 1.1.0 or newer.
- Try: `Run the probe for the next unchecked criterion in this phase and show me its receipt.`

## bstack 0.12.0 (2026-11-16)

- A product phase spec is now its ideal state: three levels (Done, Good, Surprising), criteria and anti-criteria with ids (`C1`, `A1`), and the probe that would prove each one false. A person confirms Done and Good before building starts, and the spec stays after the phase is done.
- The Product phase playbook works from the spec's failing criteria, runs each probe before and after a change, lists the criteria a PR moves with evidence (`P1-C3`), and adds a feature to a done phase as new unchecked criteria that reopen it. When you reject work whose criteria passed, it adds the missing criterion first.
- `check-product.py` checks the new spec: the three levels and a `**Confirmed.**` line, a probe on every criterion and anti-criterion, unique ids, `Evidence:` on every checked box, a confirmation before a phase is Planned, Building, In progress or Gated, and no unchecked box in a Done phase.
- Breaking for product repos: specs with an `## Acceptance` checklist fail `check-product.py` until upgraded. scaffold-product has an upgrade mode that converts them in one PR.
- Try: `/scaffold-product upgrade this repo's phase specs to the ideal-state format`

## bstack 0.11.0 (2026-11-16)

- New `root-cause` skill finds a bug's root cause from facts instead of from reading the code, for agent-written or unfamiliar code. `rootcause.py` keeps the case (facts against a control, hypotheses, and the matrix between them), says the one next step, refuses a new hypothesis before the tactics are tried or while several survive, and refuses a root cause until exactly one hypothesis explains every fact and an adversarial review on another model has passed it.
- `rootcause.py report` writes the evidence, what was ruled out and by which fact, and the layers the agent couldn't reach as infrastructure work. `rootcause.py recheck` reruns each fact's check and fails while a bug-only signal still holds, so a solved case can gate a deploy.
- The Bug fix and Perf issue playbooks send the agent to `root-cause` when the code is unfamiliar or two theories have failed.
- Try: `root-cause the p99 regression that started when the export flag went on`

## bstack 0.10.2 (2026-11-15)

- The weekly quality brief no longer stops in a Claude Code cloud session: it checks GitHub access with a real `gh api` call, not `gh auth status`, which fails there even when access works. It also says what to do when every artifact download is refused.

## bstack 0.10.1 (2026-11-15)

- `qualitydirector` has the weekly quality brief as numbered steps (`references/weekly-brief.md`): fetch the week's CI test records, book them, summarize, write the brief from the books' template with at most three proposals, check, and open one pull request for sign-off.
- Try: `run the weekly quality brief`

## bstack 0.10.0 (2026-11-15)

- `quality.py ingest` books the test-run artifacts CI uploads into the quality books (`runs.csv`, the new `failures.csv`, and `tests-weekly.csv`), rejecting any malformed file by name and booking the rest, and it changes nothing the second time you run it.
- `quality.py summary --json` gives one weekly object (suite time against the prior four weeks, slowest tests, failures on push, flaky tests, tests added and removed, the 300-second threshold), so a brief copies numbers instead of computing them.
- `quality.py record --sha SHA` records the commit you name, so a pull_request run books the PR head instead of GitHub's temporary merge commit.
- `quality.py fetch` downloads the test-results artifacts of the repos in the new `books/watched.csv` through `gh`, with GitHub's own account of each run, and `ingest` believes that account for who a run is (repo, commit, event, workflow, start, link) and a recorder file only for what it measured, so a forged or impersonating artifact cannot put a wrong row into the append-only books. Two conflicting files for one run book neither.
- `quality.py ingest` and `check` refuse test ids and other cells that a spreadsheet would run or a terminal would obey, cells over 1000 characters, files over 8 MB or 20000 tests, and starts outside 2020 to 2099; one bad file no longer blocks the others.
- A test with both an `error` and a `fail` line in one run is booked as `error`. Books layout changes again: a books folder needs `books/watched.csv` (`repo,github,workflow`), and `failed_on_main` is the failures in pushes to the default branch.
- The recorder now leaves SIGINT ignored when it starts that way, as plain unittest does, and a test that runs another suite inside itself no longer turns the outer test red.
- Books layout changes: `tests-weekly.csv` has `total_ms` where it had `p50_ms`, and a books folder without `failures.csv` fails `check`.
- Try: `summarize the quality books for last week`

## bstack 0.9.0 (2026-11-15)

- New `qualitydirector` skill records a unittest run as per-test time and outcome (`quality.py record`), so you can see what a repo's suite costs and which tests are slow or failing. A run that is cut short, an empty suite or a module that fails to import counts as a failure, never a green run.
- `quality.py check` validates the quality books (`runs.csv` and `tests-weekly.csv`) and, with `--base REF`, fails if a past run row was edited or removed.
- Try: `record the tests in this repo with the quality director`

- interrogate: an adversary in another tool's CLI runs read-only and non-interactively; for Cursor, `cursor-agent -p --trust --mode ask`, which can't hang on an approval prompt.

- The weekly Mac job (`weekly-claude-code.sh`) also imports last week's Vercel billing: it fetches the Monday-to-Monday week at midnight Pacific with the `vercel` CLI and books it with `books.py vercel`. ## bstack 0.8.0 (2026-11-14)

- New Large work item playbook in beau-mode. Multi-PR, unattended or gated work starts with a charter a human approves by its hash, and every decision, gate answer, review and cost goes into the project's ledger, sealed when the run merges.
- show-me-your-work records the decision trail with the `ledger` CLI instead of a TSV file, so CI can check that nobody edited it. Install `ledger` with agentfiles or pip.
- beau-mode and the Large work item playbook read the agent policy (`~/.agents/policy.yaml`, which agentfiles writes) and stop at its gates.
- figure-it-out frames tier 2 and 3 work as a charter.
- Try: `/beau-mode plan this migration as a large work item`

## bstack 0.7.0 (2026-11-10)

- New `beau-help` skill lists every agent-kit skill and playbook, with how to call each one in your tool.
- `beau-help new` shows what changed since you last looked. In Claude Code it also appears once at session start after an update.

## bstack 0.6.0 (2026-11-10)

- beau-mode restates your goal first and carries it into every subagent brief, PR and final reply. It stops when the evidence rules out the change you asked for.
- interrogate keeps only findings an adversary proves with a command it ran; the lead reruns each one.
- create-verification-skill counts an app as ready only when it works from an empty data directory, and never weakens a journey to make it pass.
- Multi-phase plans run one full swarm at the code-ready head and one verifier for rebases.
- reflect never edits a skill inside a plugin cache.

## principles 0.2.0 (2026-11-10)

- test-behavior-not-implementation, fix-root-causes, attack-the-premise and make-operations-idempotent now explain the idea instead of banning specific mechanisms.
- explain-the-number asks you to decide what result would change your mind before you measure.
